title: Compose independently authorized Command Incident → Investigate Case Timeline on a single local HTTP origin
goal: Make the existing independently authorized Command Work Queue linked-Case navigation of E10-CMD-106D actually traversable to the existing read-only Investigate Case Timeline handler within one server host, without transferring source permissions, adding IAM, claiming production or creating a second domain engine.
invariants: The host routes only exact GET/POST requests under /command/work-queue and /case-timeline, delegating method enforcement to the two original domain handlers; no proxy/rewrite/auth token, no arbitrary URL, no redirect.

Command Incident CanRead and independently authorized Shared Object Linking + Investigate Case data produce only a navigation pointer. Each destination GET independently authenticates a new request and performs Investigate Case, Timeline Entry and typed-source checks; no permission transfer or trusted client scope.
A user with Command Incident.read but without Investigate Case.read can see only an independently allowed Case ID link, not its Timeline entries nor underlying source metadata.
All additional source output belongs to the original handlers, never to this router; no new Case owner, persisted object, mutation endpoint, Class-2 operation or production deployment.
Existing Go 1.26.10 work-queue and investigation-timeline module boundaries are reused through pinned local replaces; do not introduce external runtime dependencies or paid APIs.
Existing #195 and #197 SHA remain frozen and unchanged; this new branch descends #197 only as Git parent, not business parent.
Performance workload identity is registered in both strict engineering validator and policy, without a waiver and without claiming a measured production SLO.

Only the explicitly enumerated engineering-tool files may be changed: host routing benchmark adapter, strict deep-policy validation and measured source-specific security checks. No generic waiver or policy broadening is permitted.
security_properties: Fail closed if either required handler is missing; unsupported paths cannot reach an owner adapter.
Preserve existing HTTP no-store and generic denied responses, prevent caching and referrer disclosure at the composition boundary.
No client-supplied tenant/environment, principal, permission or token is forwarded as authority; only pre-existing handlers perform their own scope authorization.
Source data returned by Timeline MUST NOT be available to a Command-only authorized principal; no implicit HTTP session role elevation.

migration.rationale: Pure local same-origin read-only handler composition with no persistent records, schema or external side effects.

rollback.strategy: Remove new host route composition module; leave both original Go handlers and HTML navigation references untouched.
verification: Command Work Queue remains independently available
Investigate Case Timeline remains independently available
No object or data migration required

inputs: CAP-CMD-106 authorized cross-product links and E10-CMD-106D navigation pointer from already independently source-authorized linked Case
CAP-INV-110 owner-rechecked GET /case-timeline API from E10-INV-110E

outputs: New embeddable NewHandler(Command http.Handler, Timeline http.Handler) reuses the two existing read-only services on one origin, with route isolation and no extra IAM decisions.

Cross-module Go httptest follows a real Case link rendered by Command into the real Timeline HTTP handler and demonstrates independent source checks, including a Command-only reader denied at destination.
Cross-platform Go CI on exact commit, Linux race, go vet, gofmt, 90% host statement coverage and mandatory engineering-security gate.
Provisional on-demand engineering performance registry entry, explicitly unmeasured for live IAM and network.
Strict changed-security-critical evidence adapter for the new host boundary with fresh Go coverage and authorization/tenant negative tests; no automatic source-owner trust grant.
Measured on-demand routing benchmark policy and executable workload using Go testing.B against the actual NewHandler implementation; provider/IAM latency explicitly excluded.

One real bounded Go subprocess deep resource target for the existing same-origin routing benchmark: 250 measured operations, peak Go heap and total allocations, 512 MiB soft memory hint and 180-second cap, explicitly excluding IAM/provider/network.
acceptance_tests: Actual selected Incident HTML contains same-origin /case-timeline?case_id=Case ID with no tenant or token.
Following that link through the same HTTP host returns source-authorized Case Timeline JSON for the valid Investigate reader.
A second principal with identical Command Incident read rights but no Investigate Case read rights receives no protected Case/Entry/source content at destination.
Anonymous, wrong token, invalid Case query, invalid path, mutation and nil handler fail closed.
Existing individual handlers remain unchanged; cross-tenant/session privileges not transferable.
Exact GitHub SHA validates Go compile/unit/race/vet/coverage on Linux, Windows, macOS and engineering schema/security checks.
Global CHK-SECURITY-TESTS executes measured host Go coverage and negative tests on exact SHA, no unmeasured boundary or altered coverage thresholds.
The strict security adapter registry unit test expects exactly 10 registered adapters including command-investigate-host-runtime; no implicit adapter is permitted.
The performance benchmark registry has one measured first-party routing workload and the strict validator still rejects unknown or duplicated workload keys.

CHK-DEEP-PERFORMANCE validates the matching product-runtime deep target, known executable first-party handler and exact valid on-demand scope; malformed/missing benchmark resource metrics fail closed.
Actual Go routing deep benchmark emits positive ns/op, peakheap-B and totalalloc-B data from real NewHandler dispatch, distinct from synthetic production IAM.
